title: Types of Condition
summary: Five conditional patterns, each with its own tense: what is true, what is possible, what is imagined now, what was imagined then, and the mixed forms. Getting the tenses right is what separates a real conditional from a wish.

lessons.title: The Zero Conditional
lessons.summary: if + present, present: general truths and things that always happen.

steps.heading: What always happens
steps.body: The zero conditional describes a situation that is true in general, a rule of nature, or a result that always follows. Both the if-clause and the main clause use the present simple, and the if-clause comes first without a comma.

rules.title: Present simple on both sides
rules.statement: Use the present simple in both clauses. No will and no past tense, because the situation is a general truth rather than an event in time.
rules.formula: if + subject + present simple, subject + present simple

examples.en: If you heat ice, it melts.
examples.vi: Nếu bạn nung nóng băng, nó tan ra.

examples.en: If you press this button, the machine stops.
examples.vi: Nếu bạn nhấn nút này, máy sẽ dừng.
examples.note: the result always follows the condition

rules.title: General habits and instructions
rules.statement: The zero conditional is also used for habits, routines and standing instructions, where the general form is more natural than a specific future.
rules.formula: If the alarm rings, I leave the office.

examples.en: If the alarm rings, I leave the office.
examples.vi: Nếu chuông báo thức reo, tôi rời văn phòng.
examples.note: a routine, not a single event

examples.en: If you smoke, you harm your health.
examples.vi: Nếu bạn hút thuốc, bạn sẽ hại sức khỏe.

rules.title: unless means the same thing
rules.statement: Unless is a shorter form of if not. The clause after it stays positive, so never write unless plus a negative verb.
rules.formula: Unless you study, you fail. (= If you do not study, you fail.)

examples.en: If you do not water the plants, they die.
examples.vi: Nếu bạn không tưới cây, chúng sẽ chết.
examples.note: the negative lives inside the if-clause

examples.en: Unless you water the plants, they die.
examples.vi: Trừ khi bạn tưới cây, chúng sẽ chết.

rules.title: Zero and first conditional compared
rules.statement: Zero conditional states a rule; first conditional talks about one particular future situation. If you change one verb to will, you have changed the meaning.
rules.formula: If you heat water, it boils. (always) / If you heat water, it will boil. (this time)

examples.en: If you mix blue and yellow, you get green.
examples.vi: Nếu bạn trộn xanh dương và vàng, bạn sẽ được màu xanh lá.

examples.en: If you mix blue and yellow now, you will get green.
examples.vi: Nếu bạn trộn ngay bây giờ, bạn sẽ được màu xanh lá.

examples.en: If you drop a stone into water, it sinks.
examples.vi: Nếu bạn thả một viên sỏi xuống nước, nó sẽ chìm.

examples.en: If the temperature falls below zero, the lake freezes.
examples.vi: Nếu nhiệt độ xuống dưới không, hồ sẽ đóng băng.

examples.en: If the machine makes a strange noise, call the technician.
examples.vi: Nếu máy phát ra tiếng động lạ, hãy gọi kỹ thuật viên.

examples.en: If my sister works late, she usually eats at the office.
examples.vi: Nếu chị tôi làm việc muộn, cô ấy thường ăn ở văn phòng.

exercises.prompt: Complete the zero conditional: If you mix red and blue, you ___ purple.
exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct verb form.
exercises.explanation: The zero conditional uses the present simple in both clauses, so the main clause is get and never will get. Adding will moves the sentence into the first conditional, which is about one particular future occasion rather than a rule.

exercises.prompt: If you burn plastic, it ___ harmful gas.
exercises.explanation: Both clauses take the present simple, and the subject it is third person singular, so the verb takes the s. This is a general chemical fact rather than a single event, which is why the simple present is right.

exercises.prompt: Unless you don't wear a helmet, you will be fined.

values: Unless you wear a helmet, you will be fined.

exercises.explanation: unless already means if not, so the negative must not appear again. Unless you do not wear creates a double negative that reverses the meaning to the exact opposite of what the writer intended.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is a zero conditional?

items.text: If you touch the wire, you get an electric shock.
If you touch the wire, you would get an electric shock.
If you had touched the wire, you would have got an electric shock.

exercises.explanation: A zero conditional has present simple on both sides. Option b uses the unreal present of the second conditional and option c uses the third, which describes a past event.

exercises.prompt: In a zero conditional, a comma is required between the two clauses.
exercises.instruction: Decide if the statement is true or false.
exercises.explanation: An if-clause at the front of a sentence is followed by a comma only when there are several clauses. In a simple zero conditional, If you heat ice it melts is written with no comma, because the two clauses belong together.

audio.text: If you heat ice, it melts into water.

acceptedAnswers: If you heat ice, it melts into water.
items.translation: Nếu bạn nung nóng băng, nó sẽ tan thành nước.

audio.text: Unless you water the plants, they will die.

acceptedAnswers: Unless you water the plants, they will die.
items.translation: Trừ khi bạn tưới cây, chúng sẽ chết.

audio.text: If the alarm rings, I leave the office at once.

acceptedAnswers: If the alarm rings, I leave the office at once.
items.translation: Nếu chuông báo thức reo, tôi rời văn phòng ngay lập tức.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.instruction: Choose the correct sentence.

items.text: If you divide by zero, you get an error.
If you will divide by zero, you get an error.
If you divide by zero, you would get an error.

questions.explanation: A zero conditional has the present simple in both clauses and no future auxiliary in the condition, so option a is correct. Option b puts will in the if-clause, which is never possible, and would get in option c describes an imagined situation rather than a maths fact.

questions.prompt: If you will touch the wire, you get a shock.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence correctly.

values: If you touch the wire, you get a shock.

questions.explanation: The if-clause never takes will, in any conditional type. A future auxiliary in that position turns the clause into an error, which is one of the most frequent mistakes in written English.

questions.prompt: Match each beginning of a sentence with its ending.
questions.instruction: Pair each opening with the correct ending.

items.text: If a plant gets no light,

questions.explanation: Items a, b and d are all zero conditionals about general facts and habits. Item c is about tomorrow, so it belongs to the first conditional and needs will be cancelled, which is why it is the trap in this set.

questions.prompt: Unless is used in the same way as if not, so the clause after it stays positive.
questions.instruction: Decide if the statement is true or false.
questions.explanation: unless equals if not, so unless you call means if you do not call. Adding a second negative gives unless you do not call, which means if you call and reverses the meaning.

takeaways: Zero conditional: present simple in both clauses, for rules, laws, habits and instructions.
No will and no past tense; the situation is true in general.
unless means if not and is followed by a positive clause.
Adding will to the main clause turns it into the first conditional.

lessons.title: The First Conditional: Real and Most Likely
lessons.summary: if + present, will: a real future possibility.

steps.heading: What is likely to happen
steps.body: The first conditional describes a situation in the future that the speaker believes is possible or likely. It is the conditional of real plans, predictions and promises.

rules.title: Present simple in the if-clause, will in the main clause
rules.statement: The if-clause uses the present simple even though it is about the future, and the main clause uses will plus the base form of the verb.
rules.formula: if + present simple, subject + will + base verb

examples.en: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.
examples.vi: Nếu ngày mai trời mưa, chúng tôi sẽ ở nhà.
examples.note: present in the condition, will in the result

examples.en: If you help me, I will help you.
examples.vi: Nếu bạn giúp tôi, tôi sẽ giúp bạn.
examples.note: a promise, so this is a real condition

rules.title: Never put will in the if-clause
rules.statement: The if-clause never takes will, will not or any other future auxiliary. This is not a style preference; it is ungrammatical.
rules.formula: not If you will come, but If you come

examples.en: If you come early, we will have time to talk.
examples.vi: Nếu bạn đến sớm, chúng ta sẽ có thời gian để nói chuyện.

examples.en: She will call you if you arrive early.
examples.vi: Cô ấy sẽ gọi cho bạn nếu bạn đến sớm.
examples.note: when the if-clause comes last, the comma is optional

rules.title: Imperative for requests and instructions
rules.statement: When the if-clause asks for something, the main clause is an imperative with no subject and no will.
rules.formula: If you are tired, go to bed early.

examples.en: If you are tired, go to bed early.
examples.vi: Nếu bạn mệt, hãy đi ngủ sớm.

examples.en: If the parcel does not arrive, let me know.
examples.vi: Nếu bưu kiện không đến, hãy báo cho tôi biết.
examples.note: let me know is an imperative with a follow-up object

rules.title: Other future forms in the main clause
rules.statement: The main clause may use going to, the present continuous or the present simple for timetabled events, as long as the meaning stays possible.
rules.formula: If we hurry, we are going to miss the train.

examples.en: If we leave now, we are going to miss the train.
examples.vi: Nếu chúng ta rời đi ngay, chúng ta sẽ lỡ mất tàu.
examples.note: going to for a prediction based on present evidence

examples.en: If you call the hotel, they will tell you the price.
examples.vi: Nếu bạn gọi khách sạn, họ sẽ nói cho bạn giá phòng.
examples.note: simple statement about a likely future

examples.en: If you heat the soup too much, it will taste too salty.
examples.vi: Nếu bạn hâm món súp quá lâu, nó sẽ mặn quá.

examples.en: If I win the scholarship, I will study in Canada.
examples.vi: Nếu tôi giành được học bổng, tôi sẽ học ở Canada.

examples.en: If she passes the interview, they will offer her the job.
examples.vi: Nếu cô ấy vượt qua phỏng vấn, họ sẽ cho cô ấy công việc.

examples.en: If the road is blocked, take the other route.
examples.vi: Nếu đường bị chặn, hãy đi tuyến khác.

exercises.prompt: Complete the first conditional: If you study hard, you ___ pass the exam.
exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct verb form.
exercises.explanation: The first conditional needs will plus the base form in the main clause. would belongs to the second conditional, which describes an imagined rather than a likely situation, and would have describes an imagined past.

exercises.prompt: Type the full verb phrase: If you phone me tonight, I ___ call you back.
exercises.explanation: The main clause of a first conditional is will plus the base form, with no to in between. will to call is a common error, and I call back would describe a habit rather than this single future event.

exercises.prompt: If you will study every evening, your English will improve.

values: If you study every evening, your English will improve.

exercises.explanation: The if-clause takes the present simple, never will. Remove will from the condition and keep it in the result, which is the normal shape of the first conditional.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses the first conditional correctly with an imperative main clause?

items.text: If you feel ill, stay in bed.
If you will feel ill, stay in bed.
If you would feel ill, you stay in bed.

exercises.explanation: When the speaker is asking or advising, the main clause is an imperative with no subject and no auxiliary. The if-clause still uses the present simple, so feel is correct.

exercises.prompt: Build the first conditional: if / you / lock / the / door / , / nobody / will / come / in
exercises.explanation: The condition comes first in its full if + subject + verb order, then the main clause. Putting will into the first group, as in if you will lock, is the trap that this ordering exercise trains you to avoid.

audio.text: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.

acceptedAnswers: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.
items.hint: present in the condition, will in the result
items.translation: Nếu ngày mai trời mưa, chúng tôi sẽ ở nhà.

audio.text: If you help me, I will help you.

acceptedAnswers: If you help me, I will help you.
items.translation: Nếu bạn giúp tôi, tôi sẽ giúp bạn.

audio.text: If the road is blocked, take the other route.

acceptedAnswers: If the road is blocked, take the other route.
items.translation: Nếu đường bị chặn, hãy đi tuyến khác.

audio.text: She will call you if you arrive before six.

acceptedAnswers: She will call you if you arrive before six.
items.translation: Cô ấy sẽ gọi cho bạn nếu bạn đến trước sáu giờ.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.instruction: Choose the correct sentence.

items.text: If she does not arrive soon, we will start without her.
If she will not arrive soon, we will start without her.
If she did not arrive soon, we started without her.

questions.explanation: The negated if-clause takes does not, not will not, because the condition is present in form. Option c is the third conditional about a past event.

questions.prompt: If we will hurry, we will catch the last train.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence correctly.

values: If we hurry, we will catch the last train.

questions.explanation: Both clauses cannot take will. The condition uses the present simple hurry and the result keeps will catch, which is the only arrangement the first conditional allows.

questions.prompt: Match each if-clause with its most likely main clause.
questions.instruction: Pair each condition with the correct result.

items.matchKey: I will buy a new car.

values.d: I will buy a new car.

questions.explanation: Each result is a plausible future consequence of its condition. Option b uses an imperative, which is the shape you want when giving an instruction rather than making a prediction.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: If the shop ___ in your size, they will order it for you.
questions.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct verb form.
questions.explanation: The if-clause takes the present simple, so a negative becomes does not have. will not have is the common error here, and did not have would place the whole sentence in the past.

takeaways: First conditional: if + present simple, will + base verb in the main clause.
Never put will in the if-clause, in any conditional type.
Use an imperative main clause for requests and instructions.
going to and the present simple are also possible in the main clause when the meaning is a prediction.

lessons.title: The Second Conditional: Unreal Present
lessons.summary: if + past, would: things that are not true, or imagined situations.

steps.heading: What is not true now
steps.body: The second conditional describes a situation in the present that is either untrue or unlikely. The if-clause uses the past simple and the main clause uses would plus the base form.

rules.title: Past simple in the condition, would in the result
rules.statement: The if-clause takes a past tense, usually the past simple, and the main clause takes would plus the base form of the verb.
rules.formula: if + past simple, subject + would + base verb

examples.en: If I had more time, I would learn another language.
examples.vi: Nếu tôi có nhiều thời gian hơn, tôi sẽ học thêm một ngôn ngữ.
examples.note: the present situation is not true

examples.en: If he lived nearer, he would walk to work.
examples.vi: Nếu anh ấy sống gần hơn, anh ấy sẽ đi bộ đi làm.

rules.title: were for every person in the if-clause
rules.statement: In the second conditional use were for I, he, she and it as well as for you, they and we. This is subjunctive form and it is not optional at exam level.
rules.formula: If I were you, I would take the job.

examples.en: If I were you, I would apologise immediately.
examples.vi: Nếu tôi là bạn, tôi sẽ xin lỗi ngay lập tức.

examples.en: If she were here, she would know what to do.
examples.vi: Nếu cô ấy ở đây, cô ấy sẽ biết phải làm gì.

rules.title: If only, I hope and would rather
rules.statement: would rather compares two options and takes a base verb: I would rather walk than take a taxi.
rules.formula: If only I had asked her! / I would rather stay at home.

examples.en: If only I had asked her earlier.
examples.vi: Giá mà tôi đã hỏi bà ấy sớm hơn.
examples.note: an unmet wish about the present

examples.en: I would rather walk than take a taxi in this rain.
examples.vi: Tôi thà đi bộ còn hơn bắt xe taxi trong cơn mưa này.
examples.note: preference, base verb after would rather

rules.title: What if for possibilities
rules.statement: What if opens a question about a situation that might happen. It is followed by the second conditional pattern.
rules.formula: What if we lost the job?

examples.en: What if we lost our jobs tomorrow?
examples.vi: Lỡ may ra ngày mai chúng ta mất việc thì sao?
examples.note: past simple even though the situation is future

examples.en: What if the meeting was cancelled?
examples.vi: Lỡ cuộc họp bị hủy thì sao?
examples.note: the second conditional form inside the question

examples.en: If I were the mayor, I would build more parks.
examples.vi: Nếu tôi làm thị trưởng, tôi sẽ xây nhiều công viên hơn.

examples.en: She would look after my cat if I asked her nicely.
examples.vi: Cô ấy sẽ trông nom mèo của tôi nếu tôi nhờ lịch sự.

examples.en: If we drove faster, we would arrive earlier.
examples.vi: Nếu chúng ta lái nhanh hơn, chúng ta sẽ đến sớm hơn.

examples.en: If he asked me, I would say yes.
examples.vi: Nếu anh ấy hỏi tôi, tôi sẽ nói có.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second conditional: If I ___ you, I would accept the offer.
exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct verb form.
exercises.explanation: were is the preferred subjunctive form for every person, and was is widely accepted in speech and informal writing. am and will be do not belong to the second conditional.

exercises.prompt: Type the complete verb phrase: If we had a car, we ___ not need a taxi.
exercises.explanation: The main clause of a second conditional uses would, which takes the negative not after it: would not need. Putting not before would is only correct with a contracted form and a different structure, and would to need is never possible.

exercises.prompt: If I will have more time, I would learn to play the guitar.

values: If I had more time, I would learn to play the guitar.

exercises.explanation: The second conditional if-clause takes a past tense, not a future one. Two things were wrong here: will in the condition and will instead of had in the past form of have.

exercises.prompt: Match each if-clause with its main clause.
exercises.instruction: Pair every if-clause with the correct main clause.

items.text: If we had a bigger flat,

items.matchKey: I would lend her my notes.

values.d: I would lend her my notes.

exercises.explanation: Each main clause uses would or could plus the base form, which is the second conditional shape. A past tense in any main clause here would make the sentence a third conditional instead.

exercises.prompt: In the second conditional, was is correct with every subject except I and you.
exercises.instruction: Decide if the statement is true or false.
exercises.explanation: were is the form used for all persons in formal written English, and only the plural pronouns and you commonly keep was in everyday speech. The statement gets the pattern backwards.

audio.text: If I were you, I would apologise immediately.

acceptedAnswers: If I were you, I would apologise immediately.
items.translation: Nếu tôi là bạn, tôi sẽ xin lỗi ngay lập tức.

audio.text: If we had more time, we would visit the old town.

acceptedAnswers: If we had more time, we would visit the old town.
items.translation: Nếu chúng ta có nhiều thời gian hơn, chúng ta sẽ ghé phố cổ.

audio.text: She would look after my cat if I asked her.

acceptedAnswers: She would look after my cat if I asked her.
items.translation: Cô ấy sẽ trông nom mèo của tôi nếu tôi nhờ cô ấy.

audio.text: I would rather walk than take a taxi.

acceptedAnswers: I would rather walk than take a taxi.
items.translation: Tôi thà đi bộ còn hơn đi xe taxi.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.instruction: Choose the correct sentence.

items.text: If I was a bird, I would fly south every winter.
If I were a bird, I will fly south every winter.
If I am a bird, I would fly south every winter.

questions.explanation: Both were and was are acceptable with I, and the main clause must be would fly. will in the main clause turns it into a statement of fact and am in the if-clause is not the second conditional shape.

questions.prompt: If you would live here, you would complain about the noise.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence correctly.

values: If you lived here, you would complain about the noise.

questions.explanation: No conditional type ever puts would in the if-clause. The second conditional uses a past tense there, so lived replaces would live.

questions.prompt: Complete the second conditional: What if the shop ___ open on Sundays?
questions.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct verb form.
questions.explanation: What if takes the second conditional pattern, so the verb is a past form even though the situation is in the future. were is preferred and was is accepted.

questions.prompt: The second conditional is used for situations that are true but the speaker prefers to imagine otherwise.
questions.instruction: Decide if the statement is true or false.
questions.explanation: The second conditional describes something untrue or unlikely now. Situations that are true are expressed with the zero or first conditional, so the statement describes a use the second conditional does not have.

takeaways: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + base verb, for things that are not true now.
Use were for every subject in formal English: If I were you.
would rather plus a base verb compares preferences; If only expresses an unmet wish.
What if takes the second conditional shape even when the situation is in the future.

lessons.title: The Third Conditional: Unreal Past
lessons.summary: if + had done, would have done: regret about the past.

steps.heading: What did not happen
steps.body: The third conditional looks back at a past situation that did not happen, or could not happen, and imagines the result. It is almost always about regret, criticism or blame.

rules.title: Past perfect in the condition, would have plus past participle
rules.statement: The if-clause uses had plus the past participle and the main clause uses would have plus the past participle.
rules.formula: if + had + past participle, subject + would have + past participle

examples.en: If I had known about the meeting, I would have come.
examples.vi: Nếu tôi biết về cuộc họp, tôi đã đến rồi.
examples.note: the information did not reach me

examples.en: If she had left earlier, she would have caught the bus.
examples.vi: Nếu cô ấy rời đi sớm hơn, cô ấy đã kịp xe buýt.

rules.title: The condition is always past
rules.statement: The third conditional refers to a time before now. You cannot use it for a future situation, however far away.
rules.formula: not If I will have left, but If I had left

examples.en: If he had studied, he would have passed.
examples.vi: Nếu anh ấy đã học, anh ấy đã vượt qua rồi.

examples.en: If she had not fallen, she would not have broken her arm.
examples.vi: Nếu cô ấy không ngã, cô ấy đã không gãy tay.

rules.title: Had without if
rules.statement: If can be left out when the subject of the if-clause and the main clause are the same: Had I known, I would have called.
rules.formula: Had I known about it, I would have called you.

examples.en: Had I known about the delay, I would have taken another train.
examples.vi: Giá mà tôi biết chuyện hoãn, tôi đã đi tàu khác.
examples.note: the if is omitted, the order is inverted

examples.en: Had she asked me, I would have helped her.
examples.vi: Nếu cô ấy hỏi tôi, tôi đã giúp cô ấy rồi.

rules.title: Short answers and mixed feelings
rules.statement: A short answer drops the if-clause: If you had told me, I would have helped. You would have, would you not?
rules.formula: I would have helped you, but you did not ask.

examples.en: You would have passed, but you did not revise.
examples.vi: Bạn đã có thể vượt qua, nhưng bạn đã không ôn tập.
examples.note: the second clause is a criticism in the present

examples.en: If they had asked us, we would have said yes immediately.
examples.vi: Nếu họ hỏi chúng tôi, chúng tôi đã đồng ý ngay lập tức.
examples.note: a regret about something that did not happen

examples.en: If I had known about the delay, I would have caught the earlier train.
examples.vi: Nếu tôi biết chuyện hoãn, tôi đã kịp chuyến tàu sớm hơn.

examples.en: Had we booked earlier, the rooms would have been cheaper.
examples.vi: Giá mà chúng ta đặt sớm hơn, phòng đã rẻ hơn.

examples.en: She would have told you, if you had asked her.
examples.vi: Cô ấy đã nói cho bạn biết, nếu bạn hỏi cô ấy.
examples.note: if-clause at the end with a comma

examples.en: We would have helped, but nobody told us.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi đã giúp được, nhưng không ai báo chúng tôi.
examples.note: a regret about something that did not happen

exercises.prompt: Complete the third conditional: If they had left earlier, they ___ the flight.
exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct verb form.
exercises.explanation: The main clause of the third conditional is would have plus the past participle. would catch belongs to the second conditional and had caught would put the whole sentence in the if-clause.

exercises.prompt: Type the complete verb phrase: If I had seen the message, I ___ replied.
exercises.explanation: would have plus the past participle replied is the third conditional result. A bare would replied is ungrammatical, and would have to reply is another frequent error from translating the Vietnamese da.

exercises.prompt: If I would have known, I would have called you sooner.

values: If I had known, I would have called you sooner.

exercises.explanation: would is never used in an if-clause, so the condition must be had known. The result keeps would have called, which is the correct third conditional shape.

exercises.prompt: Had you locked the door, nothing would have happened.
exercises.instruction: Rewrite the sentence without the omitted if.

values: If you had locked the door, nothing would have happened.

exercises.explanation: Inverting the subject and had is only correct when the if is left out. Adding the word if back requires normal word order, so you would not write If you had had locked the door.

exercises.prompt: Match each if-clause with the main clause that completes the third conditional.
exercises.instruction: Pair every if-clause with the correct main clause.

items.matchKey: I would have lent him the book.
I would have brought an umbrella.

items.text: If they had checked the map,
items.matchKey: they would not have got lost.
we would have seen the show.

values.a: I would have lent him the book.
values.b: I would have brought an umbrella.
values.c: they would not have got lost.
values.d: we would have seen the show.

exercises.explanation: Every main clause uses would have plus the past participle, and the negative form is would not have. Reading the pair aloud makes the regret in each one obvious, which is the tone the third conditional always carries.

audio.text: If I had known about the meeting, I would have come.

acceptedAnswers: If I had known about the meeting, I would have come.
items.hint: had known plus would have come
items.translation: Nếu tôi biết về cuộc họp, tôi đã đến rồi.

audio.text: Had we booked earlier, the rooms would have been cheaper.

acceptedAnswers: Had we booked earlier, the rooms would have been cheaper.
items.translation: Giá mà chúng ta đặt sớm hơn, phòng đã rẻ hơn.

audio.text: She would have told you, if you had asked her.

acceptedAnswers: She would have told you, if you had asked her.
items.translation: Cô ấy đã nói cho bạn biết, nếu bạn đã hỏi cô ấy.

audio.text: We would have helped, but nobody told us.

acceptedAnswers: We would have helped, but nobody told us.
items.translation: Chúng tôi đã giúp được, nhưng không ai báo chúng tôi.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.instruction: Choose the correct sentence.

items.text: If we had left earlier, we would have caught the show.
If we had left earlier, we would caught the show.
If we left earlier, we would have caught the show.

questions.explanation: Both halves of a third conditional need the perfect forms: had left in the condition and would have caught in the result. Mixing a simple past with a perfect is the most common error in this pattern.

questions.prompt: If she had not been tired, she would have come to the party.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence with a negative result instead of a negative condition.

values: If she had been tired, she would not have come to the party.

questions.explanation: Moving the negation from the condition to the result reverses the meaning. This is a genuinely useful exercise because it shows that the position of not in a conditional changes what the sentence says.

questions.prompt: Match each regret with the sentence that expresses it.
questions.instruction: Pair each situation with the correct conditional sentence.

items.text: You did not study, so you failed.
items.matchKey: If you had studied, you would not have failed.

items.text: Nobody warned her, so she was late.
items.matchKey: If she had been warned, she would not have been late.

items.text: He arrived late, so he missed the bus.
items.matchKey: If he had arrived earlier, he would not have missed the bus.

values.a: If you had studied, you would not have failed.
values.b: If she had been warned, she would not have been late.
values.c: If he had arrived earlier, he would not have missed the bus.

questions.explanation: The third conditional rewrites a real past failure as an imagined change in the past, so the result becomes negative. Each pair keeps the same time reference, which is what makes the regret work.

questions.prompt: The third conditional can describe a future situation that has not happened yet.
questions.instruction: Decide if the statement is true or false.
questions.explanation: The third conditional always looks back at a time before now. A future situation belongs to the first or second conditional, and looking forward to a past event uses would plus a bare infinitive, as in I would do it again tomorrow.

takeaways: Third conditional: if + had + past participle, would have + past participle.
It always refers to a past situation that did not happen.
If can be dropped when the two subjects are the same: Had I known, I would have called.
The tone is regret or criticism, which is why it appears so often in speech about past failures.

lessons.title: Mixed Conditionals
lessons.summary: A past cause with a present result: the most useful and most neglected conditional.

steps.heading: Two different times in one sentence
steps.body: A mixed conditional uses the third conditional in one clause and the second conditional in the other. It says that something true in the past causes a situation that is still true in the present.

rules.title: Past cause, present result
rules.statement: The most common mixed conditional has had plus past participle in the if-clause and would plus base verb in the main clause. The cause is in the past, the result is now.
rules.formula: If + had + past participle, subject + would + base verb

examples.en: If I had studied medicine, I would be working in a hospital now.
examples.vi: Nếu tôi đã học y, tôi đang làm việc ở bệnh viện rồi.

examples.en: If she had taken the job in Hue, she would be living abroad now.
examples.vi: Nếu cô ấy đã nhận công việc ở Huế, cô ấy đang sống ở nước ngoài rồi.
examples.note: a past decision, a present situation

rules.title: Present cause, past result
rules.statement: The other mixed conditional runs the other way: the if-clause is a general truth or a present habit, and the main clause talks about the past with would have plus the past participle.
rules.formula: if + present simple, subject + would have + past participle

examples.en: If I were more careful, I would not have made that mistake.
examples.vi: Nếu tôi cẩn thận hơn, tôi đã không mắc sai lầm đó.
examples.note: a general quality now, a specific past error

examples.en: If this road were wider, they would not have had an accident there.
examples.vi: Nếu con đường này rộng hơn, họ đã không xảy ra tai nạn ở đó.
examples.note: a present fact about the road, a past accident

rules.title: were is more usual in the if-clause
rules.statement: In a present-cause mixed conditional the if-clause often uses were even for plural and second person subjects, because the situation is unreal rather than true.
rules.formula: If we were richer, we would have travelled more.

examples.en: If we were richer, we would have travelled much more.
examples.vi: Nếu chúng ta giàu hơn, chúng ta đã đi du lịch nhiều hơn nhiều.
examples.note: were for we, showing an unreal situation

examples.en: If they were more careful, they would not have lost the money.
examples.vi: Nếu họ cẩn thận hơn, họ đã không mất tiền.

rules.title: Recognising the pattern from the tense pairs
rules.statement: Ask two questions: is the cause past or present, and is the result past or present. The answer gives you the pattern, with the same time allowed in both clauses.
rules.formula: past cause + present result, present cause + past result

examples.en: If you had taken my advice, you would not be in trouble now.
examples.vi: Nếu bạn đã nghe lời tôi, bây giờ bạn đã không gặp rắc rối.

examples.en: If the alarm had not rung, we would have missed the bus.
examples.vi: Nếu chuông báo thức không reo, chúng tôi đã lỡ mất xe buýt.
examples.note: an ordinary third conditional, both halves in the past

examples.en: If he had accepted the offer, he would be working in London now.
examples.vi: Nếu anh ấy đã nhận lời mời, anh ấy đang làm việc ở London rồi.

examples.en: If the hotel were cheaper, I would have stayed a second night.
examples.vi: Nếu khách sạn rẻ hơn, tôi đã ở lại thêm một đêm.

examples.en: If she had not missed the last bus, she would not be stuck here now.
examples.vi: Nếu cô ấy đã không lỡ chuyến xe cuối, cô ấy đã không bị kẹt ở đây.
examples.note: a past event causing a present problem

examples.en: If I were you, I would have accepted the offer.
examples.vi: Nếu tôi là bạn, tôi đã nhận lời mời rồi.
examples.note: second conditional condition with a third conditional result

exercises.prompt: Complete the mixed conditional: If I had bought that house, I ___ living there now.
exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct verb form.
exercises.explanation: The cause is in the past, so the condition uses had bought, and the result is about now, so the main clause uses would be living. would have been would put both halves in the past, which is a third conditional.

exercises.prompt: Type the complete verb phrase: If they had left earlier, they ___ the last bus.
exercises.explanation: Both clauses refer to the same past evening, so this is an ordinary third conditional with would have caught. It is included here because it is the pattern that students most often confuse with a mixed conditional.

exercises.prompt: If she had taken the scholarship, she would be studying in Canada now.
exercises.instruction: Rewrite the sentence so that the result is in the past rather than the present.

values: If she had taken the scholarship, she would have studied in Canada.

exercises.explanation: The original is a mixed conditional with a present result. To make the result past, change would be studying to would have studied, which leaves a third conditional about the same decision.

exercises.prompt: Match each if-clause with the main clause that makes the pair a correct mixed conditional.
exercises.instruction: Pair each if-clause with the correct main clause.

items.matchKey: I would be working in a hospital now.

items.text: If you had taken my advice,
items.matchKey: you would not be in trouble now.
she would not have shouted at the child.
we would not have seen the accident.

values.a: I would be working in a hospital now.
values.b: you would not be in trouble now.
values.c: she would not have shouted at the child.
values.d: we would not have seen the accident.

exercises.explanation: Items a and b have a past cause and a present result. Items c and d have a general present quality and a past event, which is the other mixed type. Getting the times to agree is the whole skill.

exercises.prompt: If you were not so careless, you would not lost your keys again.
exercises.instruction: Rewrite the sentence with correct tenses.

values: If you were not so careless, you would not have lost your keys again.

exercises.explanation: The carelessness is a present general quality, so the if-clause uses were, and the losing of the keys is a past event, so the result needs would not have lost. would not lost has no past participle at all.

exercises.prompt: Build the mixed conditional: if / she / had / taken / the / job / , / she / would / be / living / abroad / now
exercises.explanation: Each clause repeats its own subject, so the word she appears twice, once inside if she had taken and once as the subject of the main clause. Now must go at the end because it marks the present time of the result.

audio.text: If I had studied medicine, I would be working in a hospital now.

acceptedAnswers: If I had studied medicine, I would be working in a hospital now.
items.translation: Nếu tôi đã học y, tôi đang làm việc ở bệnh viện rồi.

audio.text: If you had taken my advice, you would not be in trouble now.

acceptedAnswers: If you had taken my advice, you would not be in trouble now.
items.hint: had taken plus would not be
items.translation: Nếu bạn đã nghe lời tôi, bây giờ bạn đã không gặp rắc rối.

audio.text: If the hotel were cheaper, I would have stayed a second night.

acceptedAnswers: If the hotel were cheaper, I would have stayed a second night.
items.translation: Nếu khách sạn rẻ hơn, tôi đã ở lại thêm một đêm.

audio.text: If she had not missed the last bus, she would not be stuck here now.

acceptedAnswers: If she had not missed the last bus, she would not be stuck here now.
items.hint: a past event causing a present problem
items.translation: Nếu cô ấy đã không lỡ chuyến xe buýt cuối, cô ấy đã không bị kẹt ở đây.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.instruction: Choose the correct sentence.

items.text: If he had studied, he would be a doctor now.
If he had studied, he would have been a doctor now.
If he studied, he would be a doctor now.

questions.explanation: The condition is a past event and the result is his present profession, so had studied pairs with would be. Option b puts both halves in the past and option c puts the condition in the present.

questions.prompt: If he had not forgotten his umbrella, he will not be wet now.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence with the correct main clause tense.

values: If he had not forgotten his umbrella, he would not be wet now.

questions.explanation: Because the result describes how he is now, the main clause must use would not be rather than will not be. The condition stays in the past perfect because the forgetting happened yesterday.

questions.prompt: Complete the mixed conditional: If I had bought the flat in 2020, I ___ a lower monthly payment now.
questions.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct verb form.
questions.explanation: The payment is being made every month now, so the present continuous inside would describes an ongoing result. would have paid would place the whole thing in the past.

questions.prompt: A mixed conditional can pair a third conditional clause with a second conditional clause.
questions.instruction: Decide if the statement is true or false.
questions.explanation: The two common forms are had plus participle with would plus base verb, and were plus base verb with would have plus participle. Both pair the perfect form of one clause with the simple form of the other.

takeaways: Mixed conditionals pair one perfect form with one simple form across the two clauses.
Past cause plus present result: if I had studied, I would be working now.
Present quality plus past result: if I were careful, I would not have made that mistake.
Now and today in the main clause are the signal that the result belongs to the present.

lessons.title: wish, if only and would rather
lessons.summary: Talking about what is not the case, with and without a condition.

steps.heading: Talking about what is not the case
steps.body: wish says that the speaker wants a situation that is not true. If only adds regret, and would rather expresses a preference between two options.

rules.title: wish about the present
rules.statement: Wish about something untrue now takes past simple in the that-clause and would plus base verb in the main clause.
rules.formula: I wish + past simple, I would + base verb

examples.en: I wish I lived nearer my parents.
examples.vi: Giá mà tôi sống gần bố mẹ hơn.
examples.note: past simple in the wish-clause, no would

examples.en: I wish I could speak three languages.
examples.vi: Giá mà tôi nói được ba thứ tiếng.
examples.note: could replaces the past form of can

rules.title: wish about the past
rules.statement: Wish about something that did not happen takes had plus past participle and would have plus past participle. This is the same pair as the third conditional.
rules.formula: I wish + had + past participle, I would have + past participle

examples.en: I wish I had asked her earlier.
examples.vi: Giá mà tôi đã hỏi bà ấy sớm hơn.

examples.en: I wish we had booked the tickets in advance.
examples.vi: Giá mà chúng ta đã đặt vé trước.
examples.note: had booked replaces the simple past

rules.title: wish for the future and if only
rules.statement: Wish about the future takes would, and if only expresses regret about something that did not happen, usually with the same tenses as wish.
rules.formula: I wish you would come. / If only I had listened to you.

examples.en: I wish you would call me tonight.
examples.vi: Giá mà bạn gọi cho tôi tối nay.
examples.note: would because the situation is in the future

examples.en: If only I had listened to my brother.
examples.vi: Giá mà tôi đã nghe lời anh trai.
examples.note: strong regret, same tense as wish about the past

rules.title: would rather for preferences
rules.statement: would rather is followed by the bare infinitive of both options, with no to and no subject in the first option.
rules.formula: I would rather walk than take a taxi. / She would rather not go.

examples.en: I would rather stay at home than go to that party.
examples.vi: Tôi thà ở nhà còn hơn đi dự bữa tiệc đó.

examples.en: He would rather not talk about it.
examples.vi: Anh ấy không muốn nói về chuyện đó.

examples.en: I wish I were taller.
examples.vi: Giá mà tôi cao hơn.

examples.en: I wish you would stop shouting.
examples.vi: Giá mà bạn ngừng la hét đi.

examples.en: I wish I had taken your advice.
examples.vi: Giá mà tôi đã nghe lời khuyên của bạn.

examples.en: I would rather eat at home tonight.
examples.vi: Tối nay tôi thà ăn ở nhà hơn.

exercises.prompt: Complete the wish about the past: I wish I ___ the invitation.
exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct verb form.
exercises.explanation: A wish about something that did not happen takes had plus the past participle. A plain past is used for a wish about something untrue now, and would accept would change the sentence into a request.

exercises.prompt: Type the complete verb phrase: I wish you ___ me tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: A wish about the future uses would plus the base form. will call would be a prediction rather than a wish, and calling me would leave the sentence without a verb at all.

exercises.prompt: I wish I would have known about the change.

values: I wish I had known about the change.

exercises.explanation: A wish about the past takes had plus the past participle with no would in the that-clause. would have known is the result clause of a third conditional, and a wish cannot combine the two.

exercises.prompt: I would rather to stay at home than to go out.

values: I would rather stay at home than go out.

exercises.explanation: would rather is followed by the bare infinitive with no to, in both halves of the comparison. This is the same pattern as would rather not go, and it is one of the last places where the infinitive marker is dropped.

exercises.prompt: If only uses the same tenses as wish for the same situation.
exercises.instruction: Decide if the statement is true or false.
exercises.explanation: If only I had known means I wish I had known, and if only I were taller means I wish I were taller. The only difference is the emotion: if only expresses a stronger regret than a neutral wish.

audio.text: I wish I had taken your advice.

acceptedAnswers: I wish I had taken your advice.
items.translation: Giá mà tôi đã nghe lời khuyên của bạn.

audio.text: If only I had listened to my brother.

acceptedAnswers: If only I had listened to my brother.
items.translation: Giá mà tôi đã nghe lời anh trai.

audio.text: I would rather stay at home than go to that party.

acceptedAnswers: I would rather stay at home than go to that party.
items.translation: Tôi thà ở nhà còn hơn đi dự bữa tiệc đó.

audio.text: I wish you would stop shouting at the children.

acceptedAnswers: I wish you would stop shouting at the children.
items.translation: Giá mà bạn ngừng la hét với lũ trẻ.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.instruction: Choose the correct sentence.

items.text: I wish I was at home now.
I wish I would be at home now.
I wish I had been at home now.

questions.explanation: A wish about the present takes the past simple, so was is correct and would be is used for a future wish. had been would move the wish into the past, which is not what now means here.

questions.prompt: If only I had more time, I would learn the guitar.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence as a wish.

values: I wish I had more time. I would learn the guitar.
I wish I had more time to learn the guitar.

questions.explanation: The two sentences are already a third conditional about the present, so If only can be replaced by I wish. Notice that with I wish the would goes in the main clause, not inside the that-clause.

questions.prompt: He would rather to stay in the city than to move.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence correctly.

values: He would rather stay in the city than move.

questions.explanation: Neither half of a would rather comparison takes to. The pattern is would rather plus bare infinitive, twice, which is identical to the structure of rather than.

questions.prompt: Match each wish with the tense it needs.
questions.instruction: Pair each wish with the correct verb form.

items.text: I wish I knew the answer now.
I wish I had known the answer yesterday.
I wish you would understand tomorrow.

questions.explanation: Present wishes take the past simple or could, past wishes take had plus the participle, and future wishes take would. Reading now, yesterday and tomorrow in the sentences tells you which one you need.

takeaways: wish about the present: past simple or could, plus would in the main clause.
wish about the past: had plus past participle, plus would have in the main clause.
wish about the future: would plus base form.
wish about the present also uses could: I wish I could drive.

lessons.title: If Only, Hope and Would Rather
lessons.summary: Three structures that sit next to wish: regret, expectation and preference.

steps.heading: Regret, expectation and preference
steps.body: wish is not the only way to talk about a situation that is not what you want. If only expresses regret, hope brings a future situation into the present, and would rather chooses between two options.

rules.title: If only changes wish, not the tense
rules.statement: If only has the same tense patterns as wish: past simple for the present, had plus participle for the past, would for the future. It is followed by no subject and no main clause.
rules.formula: If only I were taller! / If only I had asked!

examples.en: If only I were better at maths.
examples.vi: Giá mà tôi giỏi toán hơn.
examples.note: present regret, same tense as wish

examples.en: If only we had left ten minutes earlier.
examples.vi: Giá mà chúng ta rời đi sớm mười phút.

rules.title: hope takes a that-clause or an object
rules.statement: I hope plus that plus subject and verb covers situations you think are possible. I hope plus noun or gerund is used for things, not for events with a subject and a verb.
rules.formula: I hope that you feel better. / I hope for a quiet weekend.

examples.en: I hope that the weather stays dry.
examples.vi: Tôi hy vọng thời tiết vẫn khô ráo.

examples.en: I hope for an early answer.
examples.vi: Tôi hy vọng nhận được câu trả lời sớm.
examples.note: hope for plus a noun phrase

rules.title: would rather, prefer and rather than
rules.statement: would rather compares two actions and takes a bare infinitive. prefer takes a noun or a gerund, and rather than does the same comparison.
rules.formula: I would rather walk than drive. / I prefer walking to driving.

examples.en: I would rather wait until Friday than send it today.
examples.vi: Tôi thà đợi đến thứ Sáu còn hơn gửi hôm nay.

examples.en: I prefer reading to watching television.
examples.vi: Tôi thích đọc hơn xem truyền hình.
examples.note: prefer plus gerund, then a noun for the second option

rules.title: would rather not and would rather someone did
rules.statement: Negative goes after would rather: would rather not go. In the second option the subject and verb are needed because the subject changes.
rules.formula: I would rather not drive. / I would rather she drove.

examples.en: I would rather not talk about it now.
examples.vi: Tôi không muốn nói về chuyện đó lúc này.

examples.en: I would rather my brother drove us home.
examples.vi: Tôi thà anh trai tôi lái xe chở tôi về hơn.
examples.note: the second option needs a subject of its own

examples.en: If only the train had been on time.
examples.vi: Giá mà tàu đến đúng giờ.

examples.en: I hope that you are feeling better today.
examples.vi: Tôi hy vọng hôm nay bạn thấy khoẻ hơn.

examples.en: I would rather stay in tonight.
examples.vi: Tối nay tôi thà ở lại nhà.
examples.note: would rather plus a bare infinitive

examples.en: I would rather she handled the customers.
examples.vi: Tôi thà cô ấy phụ trách khách hàng hơn.
examples.note: the second option has its own subject

exercises.prompt: Type the complete verb phrase: I would rather ___ than take a taxi.
exercises.explanation: would rather is followed by the bare infinitive, so walk carries no to and no does. The comparison needs both options in the same form, which is why take also has no to.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct structure: I hope ___ the report is finished by Friday.
exercises.explanation: The following part has its own subject the report and verb is finished, so it must be a that-clause. hope for takes a noun such as I hope for an early reply, and hope to takes an infinitive such as I hope to finish soon.

exercises.prompt: If only I would have known the answer before the test.

values: If only I had known the answer before the test.

exercises.explanation: If only takes the same tense as wish, so a regret about the past needs had known. If only I would have known mixes a present wish form with a past result and is not a possible construction.

exercises.prompt: I would rather to stay at home than to go to the party.

values: I would rather stay at home than go to the party.

exercises.explanation: Neither option in a would rather comparison takes the infinitive marker to. Both are bare infinitives, which is the one place in English where the marker is deliberately left out.

exercises.prompt: Match each structure with its meaning.
exercises.instruction: Pair every structure with its correct meaning.

items.text: If only I had spoken earlier.
I hope that the plan works.
I would rather not drive tonight.
I wish I were at home.
items.matchKey: a present situation that is not true

values.d: a present situation that is not true

exercises.explanation: Regret and a wished-for present situation both use the past, expectation uses that plus a present form, and preference uses a bare infinitive. Naming the function first makes the form much easier to choose.

audio.text: If only the train had been on time.

acceptedAnswers: If only the train had been on time.
items.translation: Giá mà tàu đến đúng giờ.

audio.text: I hope that you are feeling better today.

acceptedAnswers: I hope that you are feeling better today.
items.translation: Tôi hy vọng hôm nay bạn thấy khoẻ hơn.

audio.text: I would rather stay in tonight.

acceptedAnswers: I would rather stay in tonight.
items.hint: would rather plus a bare infinitive
items.translation: Tối nay tôi thà ở lại nhà.

audio.text: I would rather my brother drove us home.

acceptedAnswers: I would rather my brother drove us home.
items.hint: the second option has its own subject
items.translation: Tôi thà anh trai tôi lái xe chở tôi về hơn.

steps.title: Check your regret and preference forms

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.instruction: Choose the correct sentence.

items.text: I would rather not pay the deposit now.
I would rather not to pay the deposit now.
I would rather don't pay the deposit now.

questions.explanation: The negation goes directly after would rather and the verb stays a bare infinitive. would rather not to pay keeps the infinitive marker, and rather don't pay replaces the infinitive with a negative auxiliary.

questions.prompt: I hope the manager to reply to my email today.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence correctly.

values: I hope the manager will reply to my email today.
I hope that the manager will reply to my email today.

questions.explanation: hope takes either that plus a clause or an infinitive, never an object followed by an infinitive. Both the plain and the that-clause version are accepted, and the future needs will because the reply has not happened yet.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: If only I ___ the earlier train.
questions.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct verb form.
questions.explanation: If only follows the wish pattern, so a regret about something that did not happen needs had plus the past participle. have taken is a present perfect and would take is impossible after If only.

questions.prompt: would rather is followed by a bare infinitive, with no to.
questions.instruction: Decide if the statement is true or false.
questions.explanation: I would rather wait, never I would rather to wait. This is the same bare infinitive pattern as let somebody do and had better do.

takeaways: If only uses the same tenses as wish and takes no main clause.
hope takes that plus a clause or a bare infinitive, never an object plus an infinitive.
would rather plus a bare infinitive compares two options, with not after would rather.
In the second option the subject and verb appear when the subject changes: I would rather she drove.

lessons.title: Conditionals in Real Writing
lessons.summary: Time clauses, unless, provided that, in case, and the mistakes that survive proofreading.

steps.heading: Conditionals outside the classroom
steps.body: In real writing you will meet conditionals written with other structures: time clauses for the first conditional, no if-clause at all, and formal links such as provided that and in case.

rules.title: when and as soon as instead of if for timing
rules.statement: For a first conditional about a specific future time, when or as soon as is more natural than if, because the condition is a point in time rather than a possibility.
rules.formula: When you arrive, we will start. (not If you arrive, as a point in time)

examples.en: When the results come out, I will call you.
examples.vi: Khi kết quả được công bố, tôi sẽ gọi cho bạn.
examples.note: a certain time rather than a chance

examples.en: As soon as I finish this report, I will send it.
examples.vi: Ngay khi xong báo cáo này, tôi sẽ gửi nó đi.
examples.note: as soon as for the earliest possible moment

rules.title: The present continuous for a fixed arrangement
rules.statement: When the main clause describes a decided arrangement rather than a spontaneous reaction, the present continuous is used instead of will.
rules.formula: When you arrive, I will be waiting at the gate.

examples.en: When you arrive, I will be waiting at the gate.
examples.vi: Khi bạn đến, tôi sẽ đang đợi ở cổng.

examples.en: I will probably call you tonight when I get home.
examples.vi: Tôi có lẽ sẽ gọi cho bạn tối nay khi về đến nhà.
examples.note: probably with will for a prediction

rules.title: provided that, as long as and in case
rules.statement: Formal and written English uses provided that or as long as for a condition, and in case for precaution. in case never means if.
rules.formula: You may borrow it provided that you return it.

examples.en: You may borrow the notes provided that you return them tomorrow.
examples.vi: Bạn có thể mượn tập tài liệu với điều kiện là trả lại ngày mai.
examples.note: provided that is formal and often placed after the main clause

examples.en: Take an umbrella in case it rains later.
examples.vi: Mang theo ô phòng khi trời mưa sau này.
examples.note: in case means just in case, a precaution

rules.title: Zero conditional about advice and warnings
rules.statement: Advice and warnings are usually stated in the zero conditional or with an imperative, because they describe what always works.
rules.formula: If you take an umbrella, you will not get wet.

examples.en: If you leave the fridge door open, the food will spoil.
examples.vi: Nếu bạn để cửa tủ lạnh mở, thức ăn sẽ hỏng.

examples.en: If the smoke alarm rings, leave the building immediately.
examples.vi: Nếu báo động khói reo, hãy rời khỏi tòa nhà ngay lập tức.
examples.note: imperative main clause in an instruction

examples.en: If you have any questions, please ask me.
examples.vi: Nếu bạn có thắc mắc gì, hãy hỏi tôi.

examples.en: Provided that you pay today, we will deliver tomorrow.
examples.vi: Với điều kiện là bạn thanh toán hôm nay, chúng tôi sẽ giao ngày mai.

examples.en: If I were you, I would check the figures once more.
examples.vi: Nếu tôi là bạn, tôi sẽ kiểm tra các con số thêm một lần nữa.

examples.en: If we had checked earlier, this problem would have been solved.
examples.vi: Nếu chúng ta kiểm tra sớm hơn, vấn đề này đã được giải quyết rồi.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: You may use the library ___ you return the books on time.
exercises.instruction: Complete the sentence with the correct link.
exercises.explanation: provided that and as long as both express a condition in formal English. in case means just in case, a precaution rather than a condition, and so that expresses purpose.

exercises.prompt: Choose the sentence that makes the most sense in formal writing.

items.text: When the meeting finishes, we will go for coffee.
Unless the meeting finishes, we will go for coffee.
When the meeting will finish, we will go for coffee.

exercises.explanation: When the meeting finishes is natural because the finishing is a certain time. Unless would mean we go for coffee whether or not the meeting ends, which is not the intended meaning, and a time clause never takes will.

exercises.prompt: Take your umbrella in case it will rain later.

values: Take your umbrella in case it rains later.

exercises.explanation: The clause after in case takes the present simple, so it rains. in case it will rain is a double future form that native speakers immediately notice as non-native.

exercises.prompt: Type the complete link: You will fail the course ___ you do not attend the lectures.
exercises.explanation: unless means if not and if is the neutral alternative, so both are correct. unless you do not attend would give a double negative and mean that you fail as long as you do attend.

exercises.prompt: In case and if can be used interchangeably in formal English.
exercises.instruction: Decide if the statement is true or false.
exercises.explanation: in case is a precaution, not a condition: take an umbrella in case it rains means in case it happens. If you rain is not a sentence, so the two words are never interchangeable.

audio.text: Provided that you pay today, we will deliver the order tomorrow.

acceptedAnswers: Provided that you pay today, we will deliver the order tomorrow.
items.translation: Với điều kiện là bạn thanh toán hôm nay, chúng tôi sẽ giao đơn hàng ngày mai.

audio.text: When you arrive, I will be waiting at the gate.

acceptedAnswers: When you arrive, I will be waiting at the gate.
items.translation: Khi bạn đến, tôi sẽ đang đợi ở cổng.

audio.text: Take an umbrella in case it rains later.

acceptedAnswers: Take an umbrella in case it rains later.
items.translation: Mang theo ô phòng khi trời mưa sau này.

audio.text: If I were you, I would check the figures once more.

acceptedAnswers: If I were you, I would check the figures once more.
items.translation: Nếu tôi là bạn, tôi sẽ kiểm tra các con số thêm một lần nữa.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence for formal written advice.
questions.instruction: Choose the correct sentence.

items.text: You should submit the form provided that you attach a copy.
You should submit the form in case you attach a copy.
You should submit the form so that you attach a copy.

questions.explanation: provided that states a requirement, which is what formal advice needs. in case is a precaution and so that is a purpose, so neither can introduce a condition.

questions.prompt: When you will arrive at the station, please call me.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence correctly.

values: When you arrive at the station, please call me.

questions.explanation: Time clauses never take will, in the same way that if-clauses never take will. Use the present simple in the time clause and keep will only in the main clause if it is needed.

questions.prompt: If I would be you, I would read the contract twice.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence correctly.

values: If I were you, I would read the contract twice.

questions.explanation: No conditional type puts would in the if-clause. The fixed advice formula is If I were you, which is also the reason were is required for the pronoun I.

questions.prompt: Match each conditional meaning with its structure.
questions.instruction: Pair each meaning with the correct structure.

items.matchKey: if + had + participle, would have + participle

values.d: if + had + participle, would have + participle

questions.explanation: These four structures cover the vast majority of conditionals you meet. Mixed and wish forms are variations on them, so learning these four as a set makes the rest much easier to place.

takeaways: when and as soon as are used for future time points; if for conditions and possibilities.
The present continuous replaces will when the main clause describes a planned arrangement.
provided that and as long as are formal condition links; in case is a precaution, never a condition.
No conditional type ever uses will or would in the if-clause.
